Name: Haley Murray
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

From the layered writing, I learned that my students are eager to get more information. I ended every article with a comment about what is coming next. it made them exciting for the next days piece of reading. I also learned that I love structure. This was SO easy to implement because it was all planned. Not only was it structured but it was good quality work. It made me feel like my students wanted to learn and were excited to do something different. The group I did this with was my sophomores and they are generally really optimistic about learning. It was fun and engaging! I will be using this every year.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
The moment that stands out to me was on day two when I introduced my second article. I had a group of boys who had an 'ah ha' moment. One of them shouted, "OH! I get it. Lennie was mistreated because of his disabilities during the time period!" As silly as it sounds, I was like "YES! AND WHY IS THIS RELEVANT?!" They were all excited that they were able to make the connection without me guiding them to the correct answer. It feels meaningful because it was genuine critical thinking. The conversations on days 2 and 3 were some of the best I have had all year. Having discussion stem-like questions took the pressure off of my reluctant students.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you? What aspects of your students’ writing are you most curious to explore more deeply with colleagues during our April regroup? What, if any, questions do you h:
I am SO proud of the work they produced. They even said it was some of the best quality work they produced all year. One thing I noticed that needs more adjustment is their thesis/main claims. They were a little broad and need refined. I think I can add some additional structure to create stronger claims next time. I am looking forward to exploring more into their evidence and how they are responding to evidence.
